title: Use of proton pump inhibitors and risk of hip fracture in relation to dietary and lifestyle factors: a prospective cohort study
authors: Khalili H, Huang ES, Jacobson BC, Camargo CA Jr, Feskanich D, Chan AT
population: Postmenopausal women in the Nurses' Health Study reporting PPI use biennially
funder: This study was funded by the US National Institutes of Health (grant No NIH R01 CA137178, P01 CA87969). ATC is a Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation clinical investigator. BCJ is supported by a grant from the National Institutes of Health (NIH R01 DK088782). HK is supported by a career development award from the IBD Working Group. ESH is supported by a career development award from the American Gastroenterological Association.
authorConflicts: No financial relationships with any organisations that might have an interest in the submitted work in the previous three years.
result: 893 incident hip fractures. Absolute risk 2.02 per 1000 person-years among regular PPI users against 1.51 among non-users; use for at least 2 years, age-adjusted HR 1.35 (95% CI 1.13 to 1.62), multivariable HR 1.36 (1.13 to 1.63), with longer use associated with higher risk. Current and former smokers HR 1.51 (1.20 to 1.91); never smokers HR 1.06 (0.77 to 1.46). Pooled with 10 earlier studies, OR 1.30 (1.25 to 1.36).
